title: Apple GPU M=1 packed-QKV single-enqueue comparison
question: Does prepacking Q, K, and V weights into one M=1 projection and replacing three enqueues per layer with one materially improve rotating 24-layer QKV latency without materially regressing hot QKV?
hypothesis: Holding one scalar output per SIMD group and the total dot-product work fixed while changing QKV from three projection dispatches to one may reduce fixed dispatch and tail-scheduling overhead. The roughly 1.97 MiB of unique BF16 weights per layer remains unchanged and may still dominate.

baseline.composition: Three independent Q, K, and V buffers, outputs, and enqueues per layer, followed by one workload completion boundary.

candidate.composition: One Q|K|V weight buffer, bias buffer, output buffer, and enqueue per layer, followed by the same workload completion boundary.
candidate.weight_shape: [1152,896] row-major with Q rows first, then K, then V
candidate.packing_boundary: Weights and bias are allocated directly in packed form before decode and outside the timed region. No per-token concatenation is permitted.
candidate.consumer_boundary: Q, K, and V regions are views or offsets into the packed output. No split kernel or copy is included or permitted outside the timing boundary.

unchanged_work.dtypes: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output with FP32 accumulation

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each benchmark implementation's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: The packed [1,896] x [1152,896] GPU result matches the host linear reference for all 1152 outputs within the frozen linear tolerance.
Every packed BF16 output is exactly equal to the corresponding result from three separate GPU enqueues over independently allocated Q, K, and V tensors.
The exact comparison covers the Q/K boundary at indices 895 and 896, the K/V boundary at 1023 and 1024, and the final index 1151.
Existing Q, KV, prefill, odd-N two-output, and rejection tests remain passing.
correctness.gate: All finite numerical and exact-region checks pass before timing.

workloads.semantic_role: One repeatedly reused QKV layer; secondary no-regression workload.
Rotating-weight projection proxy; primary decision workload.

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_linear.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0006 --run-id EXP-0006-RUN-001 --qkv-fusion-comparison --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0006-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.non_metric: Milliseconds per dispatch is not comparable because a fused dispatch contains three times the scalar-output work of a baseline Q or K/V dispatch.
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and workload, candidate median divided by baseline median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.
measurement_protocol.pre_decisive_calibration: One unrecorded exploratory block was used only to prove harness operability. It is excluded from the decision and did not change this protocol.

decision_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and candidate faster in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and candidate slower in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.promote: Primary workload meets material improvement and hot QKV does not meet material regression.
decision_rule.retain_baseline: Primary workload does not meet material improvement or hot QKV meets material regression.

traffic_accounting.allocated_footprint: Baseline and candidate own the same number of BF16 values; buffer partitioning differs.
traffic_accounting.comparison_numerator: The runner uses the same logical QKV tensor-byte numerator for both implementations.
traffic_accounting.program_requested_input_reads: The kernel still loads X independently for every scalar output SIMD group; fusion does not establish less source-level X traffic.
traffic_accounting.observed_hardware_traffic: Not inferred from timing or logical bytes.

generated_code_check.purpose: Confirm the candidate reuses the proven scalar-output kernel rather than changing arithmetic or reduction structure.
expected: One FP32 loop accumulator and one warp reduction per output.
One output row selected per SIMD group.
No threadgroup allocation or workgroup barrier.
The fused launch uses 288 threadgroups; the three baseline launches use 224, 32, and 32 threadgroups.
generated_code_check.evidence_boundary: Generated code establishes structure, not a performance mechanism.

profiling_rule.qualification: Profile only if the frozen timing promotion rule passes.
profiling_rule.capture_shape: Receipt-bound Metal captures with 50 warmup iterations, 100 profile iterations, and a 250 ms post-profile host idle.
profiling_rule.required_identity: Binary hash, commit, implementation ID, kernel entrypoint, workload, dispatches per iteration, Apple GPU device, and Metal backend.
profiling_rule.claim_boundary: Verify dispatch counts and GPU intervals. Named counters may support a bounded mechanism only when repeatable and semantically valid.

production_rule.candidate_wins: Accept prepacked single-enqueue QKV as the decode M=1 composition. Keep the generic one-output kernel and treat Q, K, and V as direct output regions without copies.
production_rule.candidate_does_not_win: Retain three independent QKV enqueues and do not add a fusion selector.
production_rule.always_retain: The generic linear projection remains the public operation for arbitrary M and N; this experiment adds no prefill path.

completion_conditions: Frozen correctness cases and the full repository validation pass.
Generated code matches the declared unchanged kernel structure.
All four recorded blocks pass environment, identity, order, and count gates.
The production decision follows the preregistered rule exactly.
If timing qualifies, profile evidence is receipt-bound or its unavailability is recorded without a mechanism claim.
nonclaims: No prefill, M>1 optimization, general GEMM, or matrix-multiplication result.
No end-to-end decoder, model, time-per-token, or tokens-per-second result.
No claim that packing can occur per token without cost.
No cache, bandwidth, occupancy, or scheduling mechanism claim from timing alone.
